help_search_empty_hint: Try a shorter word, like “ping” or “loss”.
help_how_body: During the match, GameRoute spots the game server, traces the route to it, splits that route by operator and compares the ping with your usual ping on that server.
help_term_ping_desc: Round-trip time to the server, in milliseconds. When the server doesn't answer, GameRoute measures up to the last router that answers.
help_term_loss_desc: Share of probes left unanswered at a hop. GameRoute only counts it when it carries on to the last hop that answers.
help_term_jitter_desc: Gap between the fastest and the slowest probe to the same hop. The wider it is, the more uneven the ping.
help_term_hop_desc: A router on the route between your PC and the server. Hops are numbered in route order.
help_term_trace_desc: A measurement of the route to a server. Each probe goes one hop further than the one before, so routers answer one by one, with their ping.
help_term_at_least_desc: The server doesn't answer pings, so the measurement stops at the last router that answers, often at your ISP. The real ping is at least this value, and usually more.
help_term_silent_desc: The router forwards your traffic but doesn't answer probes. Many routers are set up this way; it's not an outage.
help_term_rate_limited_desc: The router limits its answers to pings to protect itself. That loss doesn't carry on to the next hops, so your match isn't affected.
help_term_problem_hop_desc: The router where loss of 10% or more, or unstable latency (a spread of at least 50 ms between probes), starts and carries on to the destination or the last hop that answers.
help_term_home_desc: Your PC and your local network, up to your router.
help_term_isp_desc: The first operator after your router: the one that provides your internet.
help_term_transit_desc: The operators between your ISP and the server's network. Your ISP chooses which ones your traffic goes through.
help_term_service_desc: The network that hosts the match server: the publisher's own, or its host's.
help_term_added_desc: The part of the ping added on an operator's network, according to the trace.
help_term_asn_desc: The number of a network on the internet, for example AS9002 for RETN. GameRoute reads it offline from GeoLite2 to name the operator of each router.
help_term_status_desc: With a usual ping, a match turns “{watch}” at +20 ms above it, “{degraded}” at +50 ms and “{critical}” at +100 ms. Without one, fixed thresholds apply to the ping. Loss that carries on to the last hop that answers is always compared with fixed thresholds. The match screen details the calculation under “{why}”.
help_term_usual_desc: Your usual ping to a server: the median of the last 20 measurements taken before the match at the same point, either the server itself or the same last router that answers. It takes at least 5. A “≥” value is never mixed with a real round trip.
help_term_unmeasured_desc: No router answered the trace, or no trace was run, for example for a server hosted on a CDN, which GameRoute doesn't trace. With no number, no threshold applies; it's not an outage.
help_term_session_desc: From the moment GameRoute detects a monitored game until it closes.
help_term_match_desc: The time the game spends exchanging with one game server. A session often holds several.
help_faq_at_least_q: Why does the ping start with “≥”?
help_faq_at_least_a: Riot servers don't answer any probe: Riot Direct, Riot's network, drops every packet that isn't part of a match in progress. When the server doesn't answer, GameRoute measures up to the last router that answers, often your ISP's, and puts “≥” before the value: the real ping is at least that value, and usually more.
help_faq_router_loss_q: Why can a router lose pings without it being a problem?
help_faq_router_loss_a: To protect their processor, many routers limit their answers to pings, or don't answer at all, while forwarding your traffic as usual. So GameRoute only counts loss that carries on to the last hop that answers. Otherwise the hop shows “{rateLimited}” or “{silent}”.
help_faq_measure_q: How does GameRoute measure a match?
help_faq_measure_a: A Windows service installed with GameRoute starts with your PC and runs pktmon, Windows' network capture tool. When a monitored game exchanges with a game server, GameRoute recognises it and traces the route to that server during the match, once per server and per session. Riot game servers are recognised from the first exchange; other games need 30 seconds of UDP traffic with the same address. The status then compares the ping with your usual ping on that server when there is one, with fixed thresholds otherwise, and persistent loss with fixed thresholds.
help_faq_isp_q: What should I send my ISP?
help_faq_isp_a: Open the session in question and choose “{copy}”. The copied text gives the verdict, the route by operator and the numbers for each match. Paste it into your message to support.
help_faq_add_game_q: My game isn't detected. What can I do?
help_faq_add_game_a: At startup, GameRoute looks for games installed with Steam, Epic and Riot. For another game, open the {games} screen and use “{add}” with its executable. To follow a program that's already open, use “{select}” next to “{start}” at the bottom of the sidebar.
help_faq_service_a: Capturing with pktmon and some of the probes need elevated rights. The capture service is installed with GameRoute, runs under the Windows system account and starts with your PC. The app itself runs without administrator rights. If it stops responding, a banner offers “{restart}”.
help_faq_anticheat_q: Does GameRoute touch the game or its anti-cheat?
help_faq_anticheat_a: GameRoute doesn't attach to the game process, doesn't read its memory and doesn't change any of its files. It spots the game in the list of running programs, watches network traffic at the Windows level with pktmon and sends its own probes along the route to the server. GameRoute isn't approved by Riot or any other publisher, so we can't guarantee how Vanguard or another anti-cheat will treat it.
help_faq_update_q: Can GameRoute update during a match?
help_faq_update_a: The update offered at startup waits until the monitored game is closed, then installs only if you agree. If you start it yourself from the {settings} screen during a match, GameRoute warns you that it will stop the measurement.
help_faq_data_a: Your sessions stay in a local database on this PC. GameRoute connects to GitHub for updates and to Steam for game images, asks your DNS server for router names for the map, and its traces send probes to your games' servers. During a match it also sends small probes, one per second each: to your router, to the last router of your ISP, to the last router that answers on the route, and to a public measurement point in the game's region (AWS, Valve or Epic). These points see your public IP address, as with any connection, and each probe can be turned off in the capture settings. Operators and countries are read offline from the GeoLite2 databases shipped with the app. There is no telemetry. Anonymous sharing, which you would turn on yourself, is planned for version 1.0; it doesn't exist yet.
help_data_attribution: Operators and countries: MaxMind GeoLite2 databases, read offline and updated with each GameRoute release. This product includes GeoLite2 data created by MaxMind, available from {url}, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

settings_language_description: Dates and numbers follow the language: 0.4% in English, 0,4 % in French.
settings_theme_description: “Match Windows” follows the light or dark mode set in Windows.
settings_detailed_view_description: Adds IP addresses, jitter and probe details to sessions and matches.
settings_launch_on_startup_description: Starts minimized to the notification area when you sign in.
settings_launch_on_startup_error: Could not update the startup setting.
settings_auto_start_description: Detects your games as soon as GameRoute starts. Otherwise, start monitoring yourself.
settings_minimize_to_tray: Keep GameRoute in the notification area
settings_minimize_to_tray_description: Closing the window lets GameRoute keep measuring your matches in the background. When off, closing it quits GameRoute.
settings_version_description: GameRoute checks for an update at each launch and waits for the current match to end before offering it.
settings_updates_error: Couldn’t check for updates. Check your connection.
settings_open_logs_description: Diagnostic files to attach to a bug report.
settings_capture_description: GameRoute relies on the “GameRoute Capture Service” Windows service, installed with the app. It starts with Windows and only passes the source and destination of packets to GameRoute, never their content.
settings_capture_feature_servers: The exact server of each match, even over UDP.
settings_capture_feature_voice: Voice chat measured apart from the game server.
settings_capture_feature_probes: UDP probes for servers that ignore pings.
settings_capture_stopped: Not responding. Without it, GameRoute can’t see game servers over UDP.
settings_probes_description: Up to 4 small packets per second, only during a match. They carry no personal data.
settings_probes_floor_description: One packet per second to the last router of your ISP on the route.
settings_probes_region_description: One packet per second to a public measurement point in the game's region. This point sees your public IP address.
settings_local_description: No account, no cloud. Network operators are identified offline, with the GeoLite2 databases shipped with GameRoute.
settings_local_connections: GameRoute connects to GitHub for updates and Steam for game images. The map asks your DNS server for router names.
settings_local_probes: During a match, GameRoute also sends small probes, one per second each: to your router (it stays on your local network), to the last router of your ISP, to the last router that answers on the route, and to a public measurement point in the game’s region (AWS, Valve or Epic). These routers and points see your public IP address, as with any connection. Each probe can be turned off in the capture settings.
settings_retention_description: At startup, GameRoute deletes older sessions.
settings_retention_forever_description: Your sessions stay until you delete them.
settings_cache_description: Operator and country of each address, saved at capture time.
settings_wipe_description: Deletes every session, its measurements and the operator cache from this PC. Your settings and game list are kept.
settings_wipe_dialog_description: Sessions, their matches, all their measurements and the operator cache will be removed from this PC. Your settings and games stay. This can’t be undone.
settings_wipe_error: Couldn’t delete everything. Stop monitoring, then try again.

mini_fault_after_isp: after your ISP, not at home

settings_mini_show_description: Also from the GameRoute icon in the notification area.
settings_mini_show_error: Could not open the mini window.
settings_mini_on_top_description: Shows it over a game in borderless or windowed fullscreen. In exclusive fullscreen, Windows may minimize the game: leave this off.

games_notice_body: The publisher operator and the game ports tell the match server apart from the launcher, voice and CDNs. Without a profile, GameRoute follows the longest UDP flow.
games_add_path_hint: The .exe that starts the match, not the launcher.

process_selector_total_other: {count} programs open · those with UDP sockets first
report_recipient_hint: The recipient only changes the address line of the text.
report_matches_hint: A match without problem serves as a point of comparison.
report_matches_limit: The {count} most recent matches are listed.
report_matches_empty_body: The report is built from measured matches. Start a monitored game, then come back here.
report_content_addresses_hint: Hidden by default: your local network appears as “your home”.
report_for_isp_unknown: For the support of the internet provider
report_for_publisher_unknown: For the support of the game publisher
report_for_forum: For a forum or a Discord server
report_summary_loss: {match}: persistent loss of {loss} up to the last responding router{from}.
report_summary_no_loss: No persistent loss up to the last responding router.
report_summary_no_loss_others: No persistent loss on the other measured matches.
report_summary_unmeasured_one: {count} match without measurement: no trace completed.
report_summary_unmeasured_other: {count} matches without measurement: no trace completed.
report_match_unmeasured: Measurement: no trace completed for this server.
report_trace_after: Trace: started after the end of the session
report_limit_method: Each figure comes from one trace per server (3 probes per hop) started during the session, not from continuous measurement. Ping is the round trip to the last responding router; jitter is the spread of the 3 probes.
report_limit_lower_bound: “≥” marks a lower bound. The servers of {servers} do not answer probes: the measurement of the route stops at the last responding router ({stops}).
report_limit_silent: A router that does not answer pings, or ignores some of them, is common: these hops are marked “normal” and do not count as loss.
report_limit_loss: A loss is counted only if every responding router, from one point of the route to the last, drops at least {min} of the probes. The loss of a single router is not counted.
report_context_vantage: Measured from the player's computer, on Windows, with GameRoute.
report_context_link: Local connection type (Wi-Fi or cable): not measured.
report_context_masked: Local network addresses are not included in this report.
report_context_unmasked: Local network addresses are included in this report.
report_summary_loss_game: {match}: loss of {loss} measured by the game (packets lost: {lost}).
report_match_loss_game: Loss measured by the game: {loss} (packets lost: {lost})
report_limit_game: Values marked “measured by the game” are readings taken by the game during the match: round-trip ping to the server (median of the readings), jitter and lost packets.
report_limit_method_route: The route, the hops and the persistent loss come from one trace per server (3 probes per hop) started during the session, not from continuous measurement. Without a measurement from the game, ping is the round trip to the last responding router and jitter is the spread of the 3 probes.
report_limit_region: Per-region pings measured by {games} before the match are context: they do not measure the match.
onboarding_welcome_title: The route from your PC to the game server
onboarding_welcome_body: GameRoute spots the server of your match, traces the route to it and shows how many milliseconds each operator adds.
onboarding_capture_title: A Windows service watches game connections
onboarding_capture_body: The “GameRoute Capture Service” is installed with the app and starts with Windows. It only passes the source and destination of packets to GameRoute, never their content. The app itself runs without administrator rights.
onboarding_capture_down: Without it, GameRoute can’t see game servers over UDP. You can continue and restart it later, in {settings} › {section}.
onboarding_games_title_loading: Looking for games on this PC
onboarding_games_body: GameRoute looked in Riot Client, Steam and Epic. Measurement starts by itself when a monitored game connects to its server. Games you switch off are ignored.
onboarding_games_empty: No game found. Search again or add one by hand.
onboarding_data_title: Your measurements stay on this PC
onboarding_data_body: No data is sent. Sessions and measurements are stored in a local database, with no account.
onboarding_data_operators: Operators and countries are identified offline, with the GeoLite2 databases shipped with GameRoute.
onboarding_data_game_logs: For LoL, TFT and VALORANT, GameRoute reads the ping the game writes in its own logs, in read-only mode. Nothing leaves your PC.
alerts_during_description: “Watch” and “Degraded” never interrupt you: they wait for you in the summary.
alerts_critical: Warn me when the connection turns critical
alerts_critical_description: A Windows notification after {seconds} s in the critical state: loss of at least {loss}, jitter of at least {jitter} or ping {over} above your usual. One per match at most, without taking focus from the game.
alerts_dnd: Do not disturb during the match
alerts_dnd_description: Also silences this notification. Handy for tournaments or while streaming. Windows Do Not Disturb is respected in every case.
alerts_recap_description: A notice inside GameRoute, never over the game.
alerts_thresholds_description: The same thresholds are used everywhere in GameRoute. They apply to the measure taken up to the server or up to the last router that answers.
match_end_body_clean: No threshold crossed. The summary is ready.
recap_title_unmeasured: No live measurement for this match
recap_measured_note: The ping "measured by the game" comes from the game itself; the other rows are GameRoute probes along the path. Region pings are only context.
recap_timeline_aria: Ping and status in {seconds} s slices, over {duration}
recap_incidents_none: No incident: everything measured stayed under the thresholds.
recap_empty_title: No detailed measurement for this match
recap_empty_body: Matches recorded before live measurement have no timeline or incidents. The match trace and ping are still available.
live_idle_body: Open a game and GameRoute detects it, then measures the route as soon as the match starts.
live_waiting_body: The measurement starts with the match: one probe per second, about 1 KB/s, without slowing the game down.
live_readout_pending: First measurement in a few seconds.
live_basis_up_to_router: measured up to the last router that answers
live_frozen_body: The last values stay shown in grey with their age. The measurement resumes on the same match as soon as the signal returns.
live_frozen_service_body: Restart it, or reinstall GameRoute if it persists. Your match is not affected.
live_route_pending: The route appears once the trace is done.
live_body_game: This ping is the one the game measures itself, up to the server.
live_body_server: The server answers pings: the figure is measured up to the server.
live_body_router: The server doesn’t answer pings: the figure is measured up to the last router that answers.
live_body_masked: As long as your router drops packets, nothing can be said about the rest of the route.
live_points_hint: One probe per point, not a curve per hop
live_flow_ignored_one: {count} web connection from the launcher ignored. It says nothing about your match.
live_flow_ignored_other: {count} web connections from the launcher ignored. They say nothing about your match.
live_timeline_summary: Match timeline: {cells} slices of 30 seconds, {incidents} incidents
settings_probes_zones: Router and ISP router probes (every second, during matches)
settings_probes_zones_description: One packet per second to your router and one to the last router of your ISP. They tell whether the problem comes from your home.
report_matches_no_problem: No match with a problem in the recent sessions.
route_map_source: Positions come from router names, and from GeoLite for Valve, Microsoft, Amazon, Google and CDN servers. Riot servers can’t be located.
route_map_riot: Riot Games · region can’t be located
route_map_none: No point on this route can be located.
route_limit_note_deduced: {destination} doesn’t answer pings, which is normal. Traces stop at the last router that answers (hop {hop}, {operator}); the last stretch, +{deduced}, is deduced from the ping measured by the game.
